The JSON fixture preserves an actual Codex Luna review captured through ALA on 2026-10-07. `revenue-review.md` is a deterministic Markdown conversion of that recorded content. The static chart and its CSV visualize the same two supplied source values (12 and 10 EUR million); they were authored locally for rendering/validation tests. These files do not run or simulate an AI agent and are never refreshed automatically.

Office and ZIP fixtures (`source-document.*`, `source-presentation.*`, `analysis-type.zip`) are small, hand-authored input-format examples, not AI output. The PowerPoint includes a visible revenue statement, speaker notes and a hidden slide. Legacy DOC/PPT versions were converted once with LibreOffice. The ZIP exercises import and path handling without invoking a model.

`trace-v1-sample.jsonl` is the golden sample of the process trace, version 1 (`docs/process-trace.md`). It is not AI output and contains no recorded model text: it was written once, on 2026-11-20, by the fixed script of tracer calls `writeSampleTrace` in `tests/trace.test.mjs`, with an injected clock that starts at 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z and advances 1,000 ms per record, server pid 4242, project `project-sample`, run `run-sample`, work folder `/tmp/deep-proof-verification-sample`, and every duration given as an input. The ALA events in it are hand-written in the shapes ALA emits. The test checks that the script still writes these bytes exactly. The lean_documents process viewer keeps a byte-identical copy; never regenerate or edit the sample without changing that copy in the same step.
